reflection_question: How many times have you fallen and got back up? Count them honestly - that number is a measure of something good.
devotional_text:
We are going to spend ten days on falling.

Not because I expect you to fail. Because most studies like this skip it, and then when it happens a person has nothing — no plan, no theology, nothing but shame and a decision to quit.

**The difference between people who get free and people who do not is almost never whether they relapsed. It is what they did in the hour afterwards.**

So we are going to prepare that hour now, while it is calm.

# The Verse

> "For a righteous man falls seven times, and rises up again; but the wicked are overthrown by calamity." (Proverbs 24:16)

Read it carefully, because it says something most people would never dare write.

**A righteous man falls seven times.**

Not a wicked man. A righteous one. Seven times, which in Scripture is the number of completeness — meaning: as many times as it takes.

The verse does not define the righteous man as somebody who does not fall. It defines him as somebody who **rises up again**.

## That Should Change Something

You have been working with a definition where one fall disqualifies you.

Under that definition, every relapse is final proof of what you suspected about yourself, and the only honest response is to stop pretending and give up.

Proverbs is using a completely different definition. The righteous man's distinguishing feature is not an unbroken record. It is that **he keeps getting up.**

## And The Contrast

"But the wicked are overthrown by calamity."

The difference is not the falling. Both groups meet trouble.

The difference is that one gets up and one stays down.

Staying down is the actual danger, and staying down is almost always a decision made out of shame in the first hour after a fall.

## The Verse Just Before

Do not miss this one, because it is the honest half.

> "If you falter in the time of trouble, your strength is small." (Proverbs 24:10)

Proverbs is not sentimental. It does not pretend falling is fine or that it costs nothing.

So hold both: **a fall is serious, and a fall is not final.** Scripture holds both in six verses. You should too.

Most people can only manage one at a time. They either treat it as catastrophic (and quit) or treat it as nothing (and never change). The truth is in between and it is harder to live in.

## What The Hour After Usually Looks Like

Let us name it, because naming it in advance is the whole point of today.

1. 🌫️ The fog clears
2. 🔨 The voice starts — Day 8's voice
3. 🗑️ "Well, that is this week ruined, so I might as well"
4. 📉 The second and third use, which are often worse than the first
5. 🙈 Two days of silence from God and from everybody
6. 😶 Quietly deciding not to go back to the study

Stage three is where the real damage happens. **One fall becomes a week because of a sentence you say to yourself in the first hour.**

## What It Should Look Like Instead

1. ⏱️ Stop now. Not at the end of the day. Now.
2. 📯 Sound the trumpet — the word you agreed on Day 36
3. 🗣️ Tell God immediately, in plain words, without a speech
4. 🍽️ Eat something, drink water, sleep
5. 🔍 Tomorrow, not tonight, look at what the chain was
6. ▶️ Open the next day of this study as normal

Notice what is not on that list. No penance. No punishment. No week of silence to prove you feel bad enough.

## What To Watch For In Proverbs 24:10-18

* 💪 The honesty of verse 10
* 🆘 Verses 11 and 12, about rescuing those being taken away
* 7️⃣ The number in verse 16, and who is doing the falling
* ⬆️ "And rises up again"
* 🚫 Verses 17 and 18, about not gloating when an enemy falls — which applies to how you treat yourself too

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have been counting your falls.

Start counting your rises. They are the same number, give or take one, and the second number is the one Proverbs says matters.

**Falling is not the thing that ends this. Staying down is.**

## Today's One Thing

**Write your relapse plan, now, while it is calm.**

On a card or in your phone notes. Six lines, in order, in your own words:

1. Stop immediately
2. Text ______ the word ______
3. Tell God, plainly, no speech
4. Eat, drink water, sleep
5. Tomorrow: look at the chain
6. Open the next day of the study

Put it where you will find it at 2 a.m. — not in a drawer. On your phone's lock screen notes, in your wallet, by the bed.

The person who will need this is not thinking clearly. Write it for him. Write it for her.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I have fallen more times than I can count, and every time I have treated it as the end.

And every time, something in me got up again. I have never credited that. I have only ever counted the falls.

Your word says a righteous man falls seven times and rises. That the rising is what marks him out.

So if it happens again, help me get up fast. Not after a week of punishing myself. Within the hour.

And keep me from the sentence that turns one fall into seven.

In Jesus' name, amen.

reflection_question: Are you harder on yourself than you would be on anybody else? Where did you learn that was godly?
devotional_text:
Peter asks a question that sounds generous.

> "Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?" (Matthew 18:21)

The rabbis of the time generally taught three. Peter doubles it and adds one, and he is clearly expecting to be commended.

> "I don't tell you until seven times, but, until seventy times seven." (Matthew 18:22)

Four hundred and ninety.

The point is not the arithmetic. The point is that **once you are counting, you have missed it.** Nobody keeping a genuine tally of four hundred and ninety offences is forgiving anybody.

## Now Apply It Where You Never Have

You probably believe this about other people. Most Christians do.

You have almost certainly never applied it to yourself.

**How many times have you forgiven yourself for this?**

For most people fighting an addiction, the honest answer is zero. Not once. Every fall has been added to a file, and the file is used as evidence at every subsequent hearing.

## The Parable He Tells Next

Jesus does not leave it at a number. He tells a story.

A servant owes the king ten thousand talents. It is a deliberately absurd figure — more than the annual tax revenue of entire provinces. A debt no human being could repay in a hundred lifetimes.

The king forgives it. All of it. Immediately.

The servant walks out and finds a man who owes him a hundred denarii — about three months' wages. A real debt, but one that could actually be paid.

And he seizes him by the throat.

## Who You Are In This Story

Most people reading it see themselves as the forgiven servant and somebody else as the man being throttled.

For you, I think both characters are you.

**You have accepted that God forgave the unpayable debt. And then you walk out and take yourself by the throat over the payable one.**

You would not treat another addict the way you treat yourself. You would not say to a friend what you said to yourself on Day 8. You would be appalled if somebody spoke to your own child that way.

## Is Self-Forgiveness Even Biblical?

It is worth being careful here, because the phrase can sound like a soft modern idea.

So put it precisely. The question is not whether you have the authority to forgive your own sin — you do not. Only God does, and He has.

The question is whether you will **agree with the verdict He has already given.**

Refusing to let go of something God has let go of is not humility. It is a quiet insistence that your standard is higher than His.

That is the servant in the parable: holding a debt the king has cancelled.

## Why This Is Practical, Not Just Comforting

Because unforgiveness toward yourself is fuel. We established that on Day 13.

The file you keep on yourself is what makes the next fall more likely, not less. It tells you what you are. And a person who believes they are the thing has very little reason to resist it tonight.

**Letting go of the file is not going soft. It is removing a trigger.**

## What To Watch For In Matthew 18:21-35

* 🔢 Peter's number, and what he expected to hear
* 💰 The size of the first debt — deliberately impossible
* ⏩ How quickly the king forgives it
* 🤏 The size of the second debt — real, but payable
* 🤲 "Shouldn't you also have had mercy on your fellow servant, even as I had mercy on you?"
* 💔 The warning at the end, and that it is about the heart

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have been running a court where God has already closed the case.

Every morning the same evidence is read out, the same verdict is reached, and the same sentence is served.

**The judge dismissed this. You are holding sessions He is not attending.**

## Today's One Thing

**Close one file.**

Pick one specific thing you keep bringing up against yourself. One incident. The one that surfaces most often.

Write it on a piece of paper.

Then write across it: *Forgiven. The king cancelled this one.*

And then physically destroy the paper — burn it, tear it, bin it. Do something with your hands, because the body remembers what the mind argues with.

The memory will come back. When it does, say out loud: **"That one is closed."**

You are not denying it happened. You are refusing to hold what God has let go.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I have forgiven other people for worse than this.

And I have never once extended the same thing to myself. I have kept a file, and I read from it most mornings, and I have called that being honest.

You cancelled a debt I could never have paid.

And then I walked out of that room and took myself by the throat over something You had already dealt with.

Help me agree with Your verdict instead of running my own court.

Not so I can take it lightly. So I can finally stop carrying something You put down a long time ago.

In Jesus' name, amen.

reflection_question: What did Jesus pray for Peter, and what does it mean that He prayed it before the failure, not after?
devotional_text:
We looked at Peter's restoration on Day 17 — the charcoal fire and the breakfast.

Today we look at what Jesus said to him **before** it happened, because there are three sentences there that change how you understand your own failures.

# The Night Before

> "Simon, Simon, behold, Satan asked to have all of you, that he might sift you as wheat, but I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn't fail. You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers." (Luke 22:31-32)

Three things, and all three are extraordinary.

## One: He Knew

Jesus knows exactly what Peter is going to do before Peter does it.

Peter does not know. He is about to protest that he would go to prison and death first, and he means every word of it.

Jesus knows it is coming and does not withdraw from him, does not demote him, does not change the plan.

**Your failure did not catch God off guard.** He is not currently recalculating what to do with you. He knew on Day 1 what you would do by Day 41, and He gave you the study anyway.

## Two: He Prayed Beforehand

> "But I prayed for you, that your faith wouldn't fail."

Read what He prayed for, because it is not what you would expect.

He did not pray that Peter would not fall.

He prayed that **his faith would not fail** — which is a different thing entirely.

Peter's behaviour failed spectacularly that night. His faith did not, in the end, because Jesus had prayed about the thing that actually mattered: that after the fall, Peter would still believe enough to come back.

That is worth sitting with. **Jesus was more concerned with Peter's return than with his record.**

## Three: "When", Not "If"

> "You, when once you have turned again, establish your brothers."

**When** you have turned again.

Not *if you manage to recover*. Not *if I can bring myself to take you back*.

And then a job on the other side of it: strengthen the others.

So before the denial has even happened, Jesus has already assigned Peter his work for afterwards. The restoration was planned before the failure took place.

## What This Does To The First Hour

Remember Day 41's hour — the one where people decide to stay down.

The lie in that hour is: *this changes everything between me and God.*

Luke 22 says the opposite. Before Peter failed, Jesus had already prayed for his return and already given him his next assignment.

**The plan on the other side of your fall was made before the fall.**

## "Sift You As Wheat"

One more detail. Sifting shakes violently to separate wheat from chaff.

It is a brutal image and Jesus does not say He will prevent it.

But notice: **sifting does not destroy the wheat. It removes what was never wheat.**

Peter came out of that night with his bravado gone. The man who said *I will never deny you* was finished.

And what was left was somebody usable. The self-confidence had to go before the man could be any use to anybody — and it went in the worst night of his life.

That is not an argument for relapsing. It is an argument that God is not wasting the wreckage.

## What To Watch For In Luke 22:31-34

* 📛 That Jesus uses his old name twice — "Simon, Simon"
* 🙏 What exactly Jesus prays for, and what He does not pray for
* 🔄 The word "when" in verse 32
* 📋 That Peter is given a job for afterwards, before the failure
* 💪 Peter's confidence in verse 33, and how sincere it is

## The Bigger Takeaway

You believe your failures put you on the back foot with God — that you are now in a worse position than you were, and have to climb back to where you were before.

Peter denied Jesus three times, publicly, hours after swearing he would die first.

And Jesus had already prayed for his return and already assigned him his work.

**You are not negotiating your way back into something. You are being prayed back into something that was never withdrawn.**

## Today's One Thing

**Write the sentence that is waiting for you.**

On the back of your relapse card from Day 41, write this:

*"When once you have turned again, establish your brothers."*

When. Not if.

And then write one line about what you think your "establish your brothers" might be — who you might one day be able to help because of this, specifically because you have been here.

You do not have to believe it today. Write it anyway. Day 52 will come back to it.

## Today's Prayer

Jesus,

You knew what Peter was going to do and You did not take Your eyes off him.

You prayed for him before it happened. Not that he would never fall — that his faith would survive the fall.

Pray that for me.

I am not asking never to fail again, though I want that. I am asking that when it happens, something in me still believes enough to come back the same night instead of disappearing for a month.

And thank You that You said *when* he turned again. Not if.

Give me something to do on the other side of this.

In Your name, amen.

day_title: Falling Is Not The Same As Living There
reflection_question: Are you walking in the light about this - with God and with one person - even on the days you fall?
devotional_text:
There is a distinction in 1 John that will save you a great deal of unnecessary despair.

It is the difference between **falling** and **living there**.

# The Honest Part First

> "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us." (1 John 1:8)

John is writing to Christians. Real ones. And he says flatly that anybody who claims to be past sin is lying to themselves.

So the expectation built into the New Testament is not a life without failure.

That is worth hearing if you grew up around people who implied otherwise, and then concluded there was something uniquely wrong with you.

## The Promise

> "If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness." (1 John 1:9)

Two words to notice.

**Faithful.** Meaning: reliable. It is how He is, every time, not how He happens to feel about you this particular Tuesday.

**Righteous.** Meaning: it is just for Him to do this. Not a sentimental overlooking. The debt was genuinely paid, so the forgiveness is legally sound.

That combination matters at 2 a.m. You are not throwing yourself on the mercy of someone who might be in a bad mood. You are presenting a settled account to someone who always honours it.

## Now The Distinction

The phrase John keeps using in this passage is **walking in the light**.

> "But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ, his Son, cleanses us from all sin." (1 John 1:7)

Notice what walking in the light is not.

It is **not** being sinless. Verse 8 rules that out, and verse 7 says the blood cleanses us *while we walk in the light* — so there is still something to cleanse.

Walking in the light is about **direction and honesty**, not about perfection.

## So Here Is The Difference

**Falling** is losing a battle while still in the fight. You fall, you tell God, you tell your person, you get up, you keep walking in the same direction.

**Living there** is when you stop telling anybody. When you rebuild the hiding. When you quietly decide this is simply who you are and stop fighting at all.

The first is painful and survivable and the Christian life has always included it.

The second is the thing to be frightened of, and it almost never arrives as a decision. It arrives as a drift that starts with one unreported fall.

## What That Means Practically

**The reporting is the line.**

As long as you fall and say so — to God, and to your one person — you are walking in the light, however bad the week has been.

The moment you fall and go quiet, you have crossed from one category to the other, and it is extremely hard to come back from a month of silence compared with a day of it.

So the most important rule in the next twenty days is simple: **do not go dark.**

## And The Fellowship Part

> "...we have fellowship with one another."

John ties walking in the light to being in genuine contact with other people.

That is not an accident. Light and honesty and other people belong together, and darkness and secrecy and isolation belong together. You have lived in the second set for a long time.

## What To Watch For In 1 John 1:5-10

* 💡 "God is light, and in him is no darkness at all"
* 🚶 That walking in the light produces fellowship *and* cleansing — both
* ❌ The two self-deceptions, in verses 8 and 10
* 🤝 "Faithful and righteous" in verse 9
* 🧼 "Cleanse us from all unrighteousness" — including the parts you have not named

## The Bigger Takeaway

You have been treating every fall as evidence that you are living in the dark.

You are not living in the dark if you are still telling the truth about it.

**The question is never "did I fall?" The question is "did I go quiet?"**

## Today's One Thing

**Make the no-going-dark rule explicit.**

Tell your person from Day 28, today, in these words or close to them:

*"I need to tell you something about how this works. If I fall, I am going to tell you within twenty-four hours. If you do not hear from me for a while, that silence is the signal. Ask me directly."*

That sentence does two things. It commits you, and it tells somebody else what your silence means.

Because the drift from falling to living there happens in silence, and the one thing that reliably interrupts it is somebody who knows to come looking.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I have confused falling with being finished.

Every time I failed I went quiet — with You, with everybody — and the quiet did more damage than the thing itself.

Your word says that if I walk in the light I am cleansed. It does not say if I never fall.

So keep me in the light. Keep me talking, especially on the days I most want to disappear.

And make me faithful to tell somebody, fast, before one day of silence becomes a month.

You are faithful and righteous. You are not in a bad mood with me today.

In Jesus' name, amen.

reflection_question: Go back and read what you wrote on Day 20. What do you want to say to yourself today?
devotional_text:
Forty-five days.

If these last few days have landed hard — if you have fallen during this study and have been reading about relapse while living it — today is the one to sit in.

# Five Words

> "There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus." (Romans 8:1)

Take the sentence apart.

**"Therefore"** — because of everything in the seven chapters before it. This is a conclusion, not a feeling. It has an argument behind it.

**"Now"** — not eventually. Not after a clean month. Now, this morning, in the state you are actually in.

**"No condemnation"** — not *reduced* condemnation. None.

**"To those who are in Christ Jesus"** — the condition is location, not performance. Where you are, not how you are doing.

## Remember What Comes Immediately Before

Chapter 7 is where we started on Day 1.

*What I hate, that I do. What a wretched man I am! Who will deliver me?*

And then, with no gap, no interval, no probationary period:

**There is therefore now no condemnation.**

The man writing about his own repeated failure in one breath writes about no condemnation in the next. They are forty-five days apart in this study and about four lines apart in Paul's letter.

**That is deliberate.** Paul puts them next to each other because that is how the Christian life actually is.

## The Engine Underneath

> "For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus made me free from the law of sin and of death." (Romans 8:2)

Two laws. Two operating principles.

One of them has been running your life — the law of sin and death, which is the loop from Day 13 with gravity behind it.

And Paul says a stronger law has been applied. Not that the first one stopped existing, but that something more powerful is now at work on you.

An aeroplane does not abolish gravity. A greater force simply acts on it.

## Why The Spirit Matters Here

The rest of the chapter is about the Holy Spirit, and it is relentlessly practical for somebody in this fight.

The Spirit **lives in you** (verse 9). Not visits.

The Spirit will **give life to your mortal body** (verse 11) — your actual body, the one from Day 31 that you have been at war with.

This is the answer to Day 5. You asked what you are supposed to walk by if not willpower. This is it, and it is not a technique. It is a person living in you, working on the thing you cannot shift.

## If You Have Fallen During This Study

Read these words slowly and in order.

There is **now**. No **condemnation**.

Not when you have put a fortnight together. Not when you have earned the right to read it.

Now. While it is still fresh. While you still feel disgusting. While the voice from Day 8 is still going.

**The verse was written for exactly this morning.**

## What To Watch For In Romans 8:1-11

* ⛓️ The link word "therefore" and what it points back to
* ⚖️ The two laws in verse 2
* 🚫 What the law could not do, in verse 3, and why
* 🧠 The minds set on two different things, in verses 5 and 6
* 🏠 That the Spirit *dwells* in you, in verse 9
* 🫀 "Give life to your mortal bodies" in verse 11

## The Bigger Takeaway

There is a sentence being passed on you every morning, and it is not being passed by God.

Romans 8:1 is not encouragement. It is a legal statement about your standing, and it does not move when your behaviour does.

**No condemnation. Now.**

## Today's One Thing

**Read Day 20 again, and then write back to yourself.**

Go to what you wrote twenty-five days ago about what had changed.

Then write a short note to the person who wrote it. Tell them honestly what has happened since — the good weeks and the bad nights, with nothing hidden.

And end the note with Romans 8:1, written out in full.

You have spent forty-five days learning to tell the truth. **Today, tell the truth and then refuse to pass sentence on it.** Those two things together are the whole point of this part of the study.

## Today's Prayer

God,

I do not feel like somebody with no condemnation.

I feel like somebody who has been given forty-five days of help and has still not got this right.

But Your word does not say *there is no condemnation for those who have had a good month*. It says for those who are in Christ. And that is where I am, even today, even after everything.

So I am going to say it even though I cannot feel it.

There is now no condemnation for me.

Say it louder than the other voice. And send Your Spirit into the part of my body and my mind that I have never been able to change by trying.

In Jesus' name, amen.
